sections.h2: Who buys a house in Arlington, TX, and how quickly can a sale close?
sections.html:
Arlington sellers deal with three kinds of buyers: households using a mortgage, other individuals paying out of pocket, and investors who purchase houses in whatever shape they are in. Closing speed turns on the buyer: cash moves when the title work is done, while a loan needs an appraisal and underwriting first.

The Census Bureau counts 402,134 people in the city for mid-2025. Just over half of the homes, 54.3 percent, are lived in by the people who own them, so a seller here competes with many rentals and other resale houses.

  • Financed buyer: tends to pay most for an updated house, but an appraisal or inspection can sink the deal.
  • Individual cash buyer: still negotiates repairs and usually wants a typical inspection period.
  • Investor: prices the repairs in, skips showings and agrees to a date that fits your move, a probate schedule or a lender's deadline.

sections.h2: How did a railroad stop between Dallas and Fort Worth turn into this city?
sections.html:
Arlington started as a market town on the Texas and Pacific Railway in 1876 and was incorporated in 1884, according to the Handbook of Texas. A Presbyterian minister who surveyed land beside the new tracks is credited with the first town plat, and the post office was renamed Arlington in 1877.

Farm trade carried the town for decades. Then came the postwar surge: 7,692 residents in 1950, 44,775 in 1960, 160,123 in 1980 and 261,717 in 1990. A General Motors assembly plant began production in January 1954, Lake Arlington was built in the mid-1950s as a water supply, and the turnpike that became Interstate 30 opened in 1957. Six Flags Over Texas arrived in 1961, and the Rangers moved to town in 1971.

The University of Texas at Arlington grew out of a vocational college founded in 1917 and enrolled 41,515 students in September 2021. The school district ran 78 schools that year. AT&T Stadium has been the Cowboys' home since 2009, and the 5,000-acre Great Southwest Industrial District, shared with Grand Prairie, dates from the turnpike era. Houses built in the boom decades sit beside newer subdivisions, so an older home's roof, foundation and wiring are worth a look before a buyer's inspector does it for you.

sections.h2: What do the 2020-2024 Census estimates say about Arlington housing costs?
sections.html:
A typical Arlington owner-occupied home was worth $304,700 in the latest five-year estimates, and a typical renter paid $1,470 a month. Treat both as middle-of-the-road numbers: a house in a tired condition or in a less sought-after pocket will sit below them.

sections.h2: Does an Arlington short-term rental permit move to the buyer?
sections.html:
No. The city ties each short-term rental permit to one owner and one address, and it cannot be transferred or assigned, so whoever buys your house must apply on their own.

Arlington defines a short-term rental as a home or part of one used for lodging for fewer than 30 consecutive days. Council approved the rules in April 2019, and rentals running before the August 1, 2019 start date were not grandfathered. Houses qualify in a zone anchored on the Entertainment District, in medium-density and multifamily residential districts, and in some commercial and mixed-use districts.

  • Occupancy tops out at two guests per bedroom plus two, up to 12 people.
  • Amplified sound and outdoor gatherings are off limits from 10 p.m. to 9 a.m.
  • Converting space into extra bedrooms is prohibited and can lower the allowed headcount.
  • Three citations in a year, or ignoring a written notice for ten days, can lead to revocation.

If your house has hosted guests, collect the permit, and the inspection checklist results before you show it. The city's short-term rental page lists what inspectors check, including smoke alarms, escape windows, a posted floor plan and a fire extinguisher.

sections.h2: What property tax dates should an Arlington seller watch?
sections.html:
Texas appraises on January 1, so the owner on that date carries the year's liability, and Arlington bills arrive about October 1. Notices of value for homesteads land near April 1. A homeowner who disagrees with the figure has until May 15, or 30 days after the notice, whichever falls later, to file a protest with the appraisal review board.

Payment is due by January 31 for most accounts. Paying in two halves is allowed, with November 30 and June 30 as the marks. Miss the January cutoff and February 1 brings a six percent penalty with one percent interest; by July the penalty grows to 12 percent. Because the lien for the year attaches in January, a house that closes in March still has to settle that year's bill.

  • School districts exempt $140,000 of a homestead's value.
  • Homeowners aged 65 or older, or disabled, gain another $60,000 school exemption and a ceiling on school tax.
  • If you sell after January 1 to someone who will live in the house, that buyer may be able to claim the exemption at once when you had not.

The Comptroller posts the calendar on its deadlines page. For a payoff on your own account, contact the Tarrant County offices that cover your address.

sections.h2: What documents does an Arlington closing require?
sections.html:
Ownership passes when a signed, acknowledged deed goes into the property records of the county where the lot sits. Texas will file a conveyance only after a notary or similar officer has taken the signer's acknowledgment, or two witnesses have sworn to it.

Pull these together before accepting an offer:

  • your current deed and photo ID
  • mortgage and home-equity payoff statements
  • this year's tax statement and any back-tax notices
  • HOA payoff and transfer paperwork, if one applies
  • leases, deposits and tenant contacts, if someone lives there
  • any rental permit and inspection records

A house that came through an estate needs the right title paper. Executors use an executor's deed; a muniment of title order works when a will is probated without administration; and an affidavit of heirship is only a sworn, court-unverified statement that a title company may decline.

sections.h2: How should I weigh a cash offer against listing the house?
sections.html:
Count what each path leaves you after payoffs, repairs and time. A listing can bring a higher price for a well-kept house, but a cash sale removes the repair list, the open houses and the chance that a buyer's loan falls through.

Collect each offer in writing: the price, the closing date, who pays settlement charges and any exit clauses. Ask whether the buyer will take the house with a tenant or with open city notices. Subtract your payoffs and carrying costs, then choose the figure and date that fit your plans.

faqs.q: Will a buyer pay for a house in Arlington that needs a new roof?
faqs.a: Yes, investors and cash buyers regularly take on roof work, and the offer reflects it. Nothing has to be repaired before closing, so compare the offer with a repaired house's likely price after your own repair bills.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Arlington that has been used as an Airbnb?
faqs.a: Yes. The permit stays behind, because it belongs to the owner and address, so the buyer files a new application and passes the city's inspection. Say plainly whether the address sits inside an eligible zone.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid tax when my Arlington sale closes?
faqs.a: Whatever is owed comes out of your proceeds when you sign, since the lien stays on the house. Ask the tax office for a payoff figure early so the closing statement has no surprise.

faqs.q: Where is the deed filed after an Arlington sale?
faqs.a: At the county clerk's office for the county where the house stands, Tarrant County for most Arlington addresses. A lot near a county line is worth confirming against your tax bill.

faqs.q: How large is Arlington by population and area?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 402,134 residents for 2025 and counted 142,455 households in 2020-2024. The land area is 95.87 square miles.
